window.name: validation
window.note: validation year to the selection cutoff; the test year is sealed

forecast_issues.rule: daily at 10:00 America/Denver for the next Utah civil day (forecast.py)

hour_index: index i of every 24-value profile is the America/Denver clock hour i

definitions.ci: EIA consumption-basis CO2 intensity (BA workbooks), tier 1 only: hours EIA publishes; no fills. An EIA estimate, hence modeled
definitions.net_load: EIA-930 adjusted demand (isolated spikes removed) - wind - solar; a grid-stress proxy, not transmission congestion
definitions.stress: net load's percentile in the region's training-window CDF (2022-01-01 to the 2024-10-29 fit, published by the fit); a stress hour is above its 95th percentile
definitions.rush_hours: each complete day's 4 highest-net-load hours (America/Denver days)
definitions.models: P same-hour persistence (baseline), K calendar climatology (baseline), W weekly seasonal, L gradient boosting; the region's model is the best of W, K, L by selection MAE (spec §6 tie order W, K, L)
definitions.skill: 1 - MAE(model) / MAE(baseline) on the same issued hours; > 0 beats the baseline
definitions.top4_precision: mean daily share of the forecast's 4 highest-net-load hours that are among the actual 4
definitions.swing: per complete America/Denver day, dirtiest minus cleanest hourly intensity; median over days
definitions.clean_rush_overlap: mean daily share of the 4 cleanest hours that are also rush hours; 17% is the chance level (4 of 24)

limitations: Validation results are development evidence: the validation year was profiled before the design, and the same window selects each region's model and scores it.

Publication-lagged replay of a revised historical snapshot (EIA regenerates files daily); real-time vintages are not reconstructed. Envelopes are assumed availability rules (spec §5); the adjusted-demand 2 h envelope is unverified against EIA's imputation timing.
Overview regions get the forecast skill and profiles only; the router's experiment runs on the four core sites (PACE, BPAT, CISO, NEVP).
EIA's consumption-basis intensity assigns imports from Canada and Mexico the average US emissions rate (EIA-930 convention).
